error: Uses one formula for the other measure
shows: The words have no pictures yet
example: A 7 by 2 rectangle with "area 18"
if_many: Sort ten situations by drawing what is measured: the inside or the edge

error: Adds one length and one width
shows: The edge is not seen going all the way round
example: "9 and 4, so the perimeter is 13"
if_many: Trace and name four sides; write l + w + l + w

error: Finds a side from an area by subtracting, adding, or multiplying the two numbers given
shows: The formula is not seen as a multiplication with a missing factor
example: "35 square feet, 5 wide, so 30 long" (it is 7)
if_many: Rows of 5 on grid paper until the 35 squares are used

error: From a perimeter, takes off one side, or does not halve
shows: One pair of sides is counted
source: IM lesson 17 (one side taken off); not halving is from memory
example: "44 feet of fence, 14 long, so 30 wide" (it is 8)

error: Wrong unit: "40 feet" for an area
shows: Squares and lengths are not told apart
example: "A rug 9 feet by 3 feet has an area of 27 feet"
if_many: Eight answers with no units: write feet or square feet on each

error: Counts the squares along the edge, not the unit sides
shows: The edge is not yet seen as unit lengths
source: From memory; teaching move Prog. p. 108 (102)
example: A 5 by 3 rectangle with perimeter 12
if_many: Tick and number each unit side along the edge, then count the ticks

error: Mixes the two comparisons: reads 'times as many' as 'more than' (5 times as many as 3 is 8), or multiplies in a 'more than' story (3 more than 5 is 15)
shows: The two kinds of comparison are not yet told apart
example: "8 times as many as 3 is 11", a 3-strip and a strip of 3 and 8, beside eight copies of the 3-strip (24)
if_many: Build both with cubes, "8 more than 3" and "8 times as many as 3"; say which is which

error: Multiplies because the problem says "times", without asking which amount is which: the bigger amount multiplied again (day 82), or a multiplication when the smaller amount or the number of times is unknown (from day 84)
shows: A key word is followed in place of the situation
example: "Jo has 12 shells. That is 2 times as many as Max has. Max has 24", beside 6
if_many: Before any numbers: "who has more?" Mark the longer strip; the answer must fit it

error: Swaps the roles: makes the smaller amount the larger (in a times story, says the smaller is so many times as many; in a more-than story, gives the extra to the smaller)
shows: Lost track of which number is the multiplier
example: "12 is 4 times as many as 3" written as 3 = 4 × 12, beside 12 = 4 × 3
if_many: Point to the longer strip first: "which amount is bigger?"; the bigger amount stands alone in the equation

error: Draws the first amount and then that many more copies, or counts both amounts together
shows: "Times as many" taken as copies added on top
source: Partly IM lesson 2; the rest from memory
example: "4 times as many as 3" drawn as a 3-strip with four more 3-strips after it (15), beside four copies (12)
if_many: Count the copies aloud, starting with the first strip as copy one

error: First idea, not an error: "3 times more than 4" could mean 12 or 16
shows: The phrase is unclear in everyday English
example: "3 times more than 4 dollars": is it 12 or 16? A talk, not a correction
if_many: Not marked. Our problems say "times as much"

error: Stops after one step
shows: Solves the part that was easy to see
example: "Lena has 40 dollars. Omar has 2 times as much. How much do they have together? 80", beside 120
if_many: Underline the question; after solving, read the question again and ask "is that what I found?"

error: Gives an answer with no equation, or a letter that stands for nothing named
shows: The equation is seen as extra, not as the plan
example: An answer alone, 33, beside "s = 4 × 6 + 9, s is all the stickers, s = 33"
if_many: Say what the letter stands for, in words, before any numbers are written

error: Works a two-step equation left to right: 10 + 3 × 3 = 39
shows: Order of operations from grade 3 is not firm
if_many: Write the two steps as two equations for a week, then join them

error: Lists some factor pairs and stops; often leaves out 1 × n
shows: There is no order to the search
example: "The factor pairs of 20 are 2 × 10 and 4 × 5. Done." beside 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5
if_many: As a class, search 30 in order: for 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 say "yes, with __" or "no"

error: Finds only pairs from the times tables: no 3 × 14, no 4 × 17
shows: A factor is "a fact I know", not "divides with none left"
example: "42: 1 × 42, 2 × 21, 6 × 7." beside the list with 3 × 14
if_many: Test 3 and 4 on 42, 45, 56 and 81, starting from ten times: 3 × 10 = 30, and 12 more is 3 × 4, so 3 × 14 = 42

error: Counts a turned pair as new, or keeps searching past the turn
shows: 4 × 7 and 7 × 4 are not seen as one rectangle
source: From memory; the Progressions describe the turn
example: "28 has five factor pairs: 1 × 28, 2 × 14, 4 × 7, 7 × 4, 14 × 2." beside the three
if_many: Cut a 4 by 7 rectangle from grid paper, turn it, name it both ways; cross out the turned pairs in two lists

error: Swaps factor and multiple: "the multiples of 6 are 1, 2, 3, 6"
shows: The two words are not yet tied to one equation
example: "The multiples of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6." beside 6, 12, 18, 24 and on
if_many: Sort 1, 3, 9, 18, 27 and 54 into "factor of 9" and "multiple of 9"; say each with its equation. 9 goes in both: 1 × 9 = 9 says it.

error: Judges "a multiple of" by the last digit or by even and odd, or stops at ten times
shows: A rule that works for 2, 5 and 10 is stretched; the tables are taken for all the multiples
example: "46 is a multiple of 6, because it ends in 6." beside 6 × 7 = 42 and 6 × 8 = 48. "68 is not a multiple of 4: the 4s stop at 40." beside 4 × 10 + 4 × 7 = 4 × 17
if_many: Fence four numbers between two products of the number tested, starting from ten times where needed

error: Odd, or "not in my tables", means prime
shows: Prime is a look, not the result of a search
source: From memory; IM lesson 3 notes only that its primes are odd except 2
example: "87 is prime: it is odd and not in the times tables." beside 3 × 29 = 87
if_many: Search 39, 57, 95 and 97 in order to the turn; a number is called prime only after the search finds nothing

error: Calls 1 prime; calls 2 composite because it is even
shows: Prime is "few factors", not exactly two
source: From memory; IM lesson 3 records the question "Is 1 a prime number?"
example: "1 is prime." and "2 is composite, because it is even." beside the factors of each
if_many: Write the factors of 1, 2, 3 and 4 and count them: one, two, two, three. Prime means exactly two

error: Drops a carry: usually one, rarely all
shows: Each column is added as its own small sum
source: Partly IM lesson 19; the rest from memory
if_many: One sum in expanded form beside the algorithm; say each carry by its value

error: Lines numbers up from the left
shows: Digits are matched, not places
example: 6,285 + 947 = 15,755, beside an estimate of 7,200 and the sum 7,232
if_many: Place names over the columns; say both numbers aloud first

error: Calls every carry "one"
shows: The place value is gone
example: In 3,746 + 2,538, the small 1 over the thousands called "a one", beside "one thousand: 12 hundreds is 1 thousand and 2 hundreds"
if_many: Students name each carry aloud for a day

error: Writes a two-digit sum in one column
shows: A place is not seen as holding one digit
if_many: The same sum in expanded form

error: Loses the last carry into a new place
shows: Stops at the longer number's last digit
if_many: Estimate first: the sum must pass 100,000

error: In each column, takes the smaller digit from the larger, whichever is on top; or subtracts from the left with no ungrouping
shows: Each column is its own small problem
if_many: Ask "can I take 8 from 2?" in every column; ungroup everything first, then subtract

error: Writes the small 1 to make 12 ones, but leaves the 7 tens as 7
shows: The marks are copied; nothing was traded
if_many: One difference in expanded form beside the algorithm; say what the 7 tens became

error: Ungroups rightly, then forgets a place was already made smaller
shows: Lost track while switching between ungrouping and subtracting
if_many: Ungroup everything first, then subtract; check by adding

error: Across zeros, turns each zero into 10 and leaves it 10
shows: The zero place passed nothing on
source: IM lesson 21 names zeros as the hard case; this form of the error is from memory
if_many: Rename the top number in words before writing: 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 15 ones
